newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish-U.S. Przymierze to launch 2 more funds '97.
newsitem.headline: Polish-U.S. Przymierze to launch 2 more funds '97.

text.p: The Polish-U.S. mutual fund company Przymierze Towarzystwo Funduszy Powierniczych SA plans to launch an aggressive fund in April and a debt instrument fund at mid-1997, the firm's president said.

Tomasz Bankowski told Reuters on Thursday that the Eurofundusz 2 aggressive fund made up largely of stocks could start selling units in April and the Eurofundusz 3 fund largely of bonds and treasury instruments could start by July 1.

"We want to start (the aggressive fund) in April at the latest, maybe earlier. We think if the bourse is in the same shape as recently that might be a good time to start such a fund -- it might be a good time to buy," Bankowski said.
The Warsaw bourse's main market has slipped 10.4 percent to 13,515.9 points from its October 9, 30-month high.
Przymierze's balanced fund, Eurofundusz 1, started selling units in September and seeks to gain an asset value of about 200 million zlotys, or 50,000 to 60,000 accounts, by the end of next year.
Bankowski said the firm thus far had less than 5,000 accounts but that the new funds would broaden its offer.
Przymierze, which has a capital of six million zlotys, is 51-percent owned by Polish state-owned Bank Pekao SA, while the U.S.'s Alliance Capital Management LP has 49 percent.
So far only First Polish Trust Fund Co., a fully-owned subsidiary of the U.S.-based Pioneer Group Inc, offers in Poland a balanced, aggressive and debt instruments fund.
